summary.intent: Complete Phase 23 gap closure execution (plan 23-08: Windows WinFsp extraction to crate), then run a security review of the Phase 23 Rust SDK crates and fix the two HIGH findings discovered.
summary.outcome: Phase 23 gap closure was resumed and completed after a subagent API disconnect; all 8 plans are done. Security review found 0 critical / 2 high issues, both of which were fixed and committed: ed25519-dalek zeroize feature enabled and `generate_ed25519_keypair` now returns `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`.

repo: Phase 23 extracts FUSE logic into 5 crates: cipherbox-fuse, cipherbox-crypto, and platform-specific variants. Windows WinFsp ops live in crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/.
All KeyState and CipherBoxFS key fields already use Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>; the project has a strong baseline zeroization culture except for a gap in the ed25519 keypair generator return type.
Callers of generate_ed25519_keypair were redundantly wrapping the return value in Zeroizing::new(...clone()), indicating the function's non-Zeroizing return was a known workaround.
The macOS/Linux and Windows write_ops both use .try_into() to convert Vec<u8> to [u8; 32] for SigningKey construction; with Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> this requires explicit .into_inner() before try_into().
Zeroizing<T> does not implement TryInto<[u8; N]> directly — callers must call .into_inner() to extract the inner Vec before conversion.
AES-CTR mode is used for IPFS content (not AES-GCM); integrity relies on IPFS CID verification which the client does not enforce post-fetch — a deferred architectural concern.
A secondary ed25519 keypair generation path exists in write_ops.rs (file IPNS keys via ed25519_dalek directly, not via generate_ed25519_keypair) that was out of scope for this fix.

code.finding: generate_ed25519_keypair previously returned bare Vec<u8> for private key; changed to Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> to prevent key material persisting in freed memory.
ed25519-dalek dependency was missing the 'zeroize' feature flag; SigningKey does not zero on drop without it.
Redundant Zeroizing::new(ipns_private_key.clone()) wrapper removed after generate_ed25519_keypair return type change.
try_into() on Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> requires .into_inner() first; fixed to use ipns_private_key.into_inner().try_into().
Same try_into() pattern as macOS counterpart; fixed with .into_inner().

workflow: When a GSD subagent disconnects mid-plan, the code commits may already be present; check git log before re-executing to avoid duplicate work — only bookkeeping (SUMMARY.md, STATE.md, ROADMAP.md) may remain.
The security:review command scopes by phase and spawns a dedicated explorer agent; it produces a timestamped report in .planning/security/ and surfaces top issues inline.
Verifying compile after type signature changes (cargo check per crate) before committing saves round-trips; running tests on the directly modified crate (crypto) validates correctness cheaply.

friction: Subagent API disconnect (ConnectionRefused) mid-wave-1 required manual resume and partial re-execution of bookkeeping steps.
1Password SSH agent failed to sign commits on three consecutive attempts, requiring the user to be present and retry manually before the bookkeeping commit could land.
Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> does not implement TryInto<[u8; 32]> transparently, requiring .into_inner() call — this was a non-obvious compilation error discovered only after the type change.
open_items: AES-CTR integrity gap: client does not verify IPFS CID after fetching ciphertext, leaving it vulnerable to bit-flip attacks from a malicious relay. Deferred as an architectural concern beyond Phase 23 scope.
Secondary ed25519 keypair path in write_ops.rs (file IPNS keys generated via ed25519_dalek directly) does not go through generate_ed25519_keypair and was not zeroized in this fix pass.

~30 test case suggestions from the security review (AES-GCM, AES-CTR, ECIES, HKDF, Ed25519, VaultBlob categories) were generated in REVIEW-2026-03-24-phase23.md but not yet implemented as actual tests.
